result.summary: The page is largely well-structured, but one restaurant card is stuck in a loading state: a spinner overlays an already-rendered image, which reads as a broken/stalled UI. A few smaller polish issues (low-contrast search placeholder, inconsistent card metadata between sections) are also present.

issues.description: The 'Tokumaru Ramen Bar' card in 'Popular right now' shows a circular loading spinner centered on top of a fully rendered (but dimmed/blurred) food image. The card's text, rating, delivery info and '€0 delivery' badge are already loaded, so the persistent spinner looks like a stuck/failed image load rather than an intentional state.
issues.suggestion: Remove the spinner once the image has decoded, or show a proper skeleton placeholder until the asset is ready. Add a timeout/error fallback so a failed image request never leaves an indefinite spinner over visible content.

issues.description: The image behind the spinner is noticeably darkened/blurred compared to the pizza card below it, creating an inconsistent look between two adjacent cards in the same list.
issues.suggestion: Apply the dim/blur treatment only while genuinely loading and keep it consistent across cards; once loaded, render images at full brightness like the neighboring card.

issues.description: The search field placeholder 'Restaurants, dishes, groceries' is light gray on a very light gray fill, giving low contrast that may fail WCAG 1.4.3 for users with low vision.
issues.suggestion: Darken the placeholder text (or lighten the field background) to reach at least 4.5:1 contrast, and ensure the field has an accessible label.

issues.description: Cards in 'Fastest near you' show only name and delivery fee, while 'Popular right now' cards show rating, time, fee and cuisine. The absence of ratings/cuisine in the first row makes the two sections feel inconsistent and gives users less decision-making info.
issues.suggestion: Standardize the restaurant card metadata (rating, ETA, delivery fee, cuisine) across both sections, or intentionally differentiate with a clear compact-card style.

issues.description: The first carousel tile (Green Bowl Poké) uses a light/white photo background while the adjacent tiles use dark backgrounds, producing a visually uneven row.
issues.suggestion: Normalize image backgrounds or apply a consistent container background/overlay so the carousel reads as a cohesive set.
